meta.title: Bun vs Express: Which one to choose in 2026? (APIs, performance & deployment & code compared)
meta.description: Compare Bun and Express architectural trade-offs, API design, runtime behavior, and request handling, and review side-by-side TypeScript to choose the right stack.

verdict: Choose Bun if you want an all-in-one, high-performance runtime with built-in tooling and are comfortable with a younger ecosystem. Choose Express if you need a mature, battle-tested framework with a vast middleware ecosystem and broad compatibility. Bun can also run Express apps, so you can migrate gradually.

comparison.toolA: Bun is a JavaScript runtime built on JavaScriptCore, designed for speed. It includes a fast HTTP server and often shows lower startup times and higher throughput than Node.js in synthetic benchmarks, though real-world results depend on workload and configuration.
comparison.toolB: Express is a minimal web framework that runs on Node.js (and can run on Bun). Its performance is tied to the underlying runtime; Express itself adds little overhead, but Node.js may be slower than Bun in some benchmarks.

comparison.toolA: Bun aims to be compatible with many Node.js APIs and npm packages, but some packages may not work perfectly due to runtime differences. Its ecosystem is growing but still smaller than Node.js's.
comparison.toolB: Express has a vast, mature ecosystem of middleware and plugins accumulated over many years. Most Node.js libraries and tools are designed with Express compatibility in mind, making it easy to find solutions and hire developers.

comparison.toolA: Bun bundles a package manager, bundler, test runner, and transpiler out of the box, reducing the need for separate tools. It also supports TypeScript and JSX natively, which can streamline development.
comparison.toolB: Express is unopinionated and minimal, offering a straightforward API for routing and middleware. However, it requires separate tools for testing, bundling, and other tasks, which can mean more setup but greater flexibility.

comparison.toolA: Bun is relatively new and evolving quickly, so its APIs and behavior may change between versions. While it is production-ready for many use cases, some edge cases and platform-specific issues may still arise.
comparison.toolB: Express has been stable and widely used for over a decade, with a predictable release cycle and extensive real-world validation. It is considered a safe, conservative choice for production applications.

comparison.toolA: Bun's documentation is comprehensive and improving, but because it is newer, there are fewer community tutorials and Stack Overflow answers. Developers familiar with Node.js will find many concepts similar.
comparison.toolB: Express has abundant documentation, tutorials, and community resources. Its API is small and easy to learn, making it accessible to beginners and well-understood by experienced developers.

comparison.toolA: Bun supports TypeScript out of the box without additional configuration, allowing developers to run .ts files directly. This can simplify development and reduce build steps.
comparison.toolB: Express itself is written in JavaScript and does not provide built-in TypeScript support, though type definitions are available via @types/express. Using TypeScript with Express typically requires additional setup and a build step.

comparison.toolA: Bun is developed by Oven, a startup, and has a growing community. Its long-term support and governance model are less established compared to Node.js.
comparison.toolB: Express is part of the OpenJS Foundation and has a large, active community. It is widely adopted by enterprises and has a mature governance structure.

faq.q: Can I use Express with Bun?
faq.a: Yes, Bun aims to be compatible with Node.js frameworks, and many developers run Express applications on Bun. However, compatibility is not guaranteed for all middleware, so testing your specific stack is recommended. This approach lets you benefit from Bun's performance while keeping Express's familiar API.

Bun has reached a level of maturity where it is used in production by some companies, but it is still younger than Node.js. Its stability and compatibility have improved significantly, yet for mission-critical systems, you should evaluate it thoroughly against your requirements. Express on Node.js remains a more conservative choice.

faq.q: Which is faster for building APIs, Bun or Express?
faq.a: Bun's built-in HTTP server is designed for high performance and often outperforms Express on Node.js in benchmarks. However, Express running on Bun can also be fast, and real-world speed depends on your application logic, database, and deployment environment. For maximum raw throughput, Bun's native server may have an edge.

Express can be used with TypeScript, but it requires installing type definitions and setting up a build step or using a runtime like ts-node. Bun, by contrast, supports TypeScript natively, which can simplify the development workflow. If TypeScript is a priority, Bun offers a smoother experience.

faq.q: What are the main drawbacks of Bun compared to Express?
faq.a: Bun's ecosystem is smaller, and some npm packages may not work perfectly due to runtime differences. It also has a shorter track record in production, which can be a concern for risk-averse teams. Express, meanwhile, benefits from years of stability and a vast middleware ecosystem.

faq.q: Should I migrate my Express app to Bun?
faq.a: Migrating to Bun can offer performance benefits and built-in tooling, but it requires testing for compatibility with your dependencies and middleware. Since Bun can run Express apps, you can try it incrementally. Evaluate whether the performance gains justify the migration effort for your specific application.

faq.q: Which has better long-term support, Bun or Express?
faq.a: Express is part of the OpenJS Foundation and has a long history of stable releases and community support. Bun is backed by a startup and, while it is actively developed, its long-term governance and support model are less established. For projects requiring long-term stability, Express may be the safer choice.

faq.q: Can I use Bun's built-in tools with Express?
faq.a: Yes, you can use Bun's package manager, test runner, and bundler in an Express project, even if you run Express on Node.js. This allows you to leverage Bun's tooling without switching runtimes. However, some tools may assume a Node.js environment, so verify compatibility.

heroSubtitle: Choosing between Bun and Express changes how a project handles runtime behavior and request handling, so data requirements, team skills, and deployment constraints matter.
quickVerdict: Bun is the better fit when your project prioritizes performance and runtime architecture: Bun is a JavaScript runtime built on JavaScriptCore, designed for speed. Express is a stronger fit when your project prioritizes ecosystem and middleware availability: Express has a vast, mature ecosystem of middleware and plugins accumulated over many years.
